From 18d78171c061889a9a43152f60d6a27a10fc7656 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2021 17:07:16 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] blk-mq: check q->poll_stat in queue_poll_stat_show

Without checking q->poll_stat in queue_poll_stat_show(), kernel panic
may be caused if q->poll_stat isn't allocated.

Fixes: 48b5c1fbcd8c ("block: only allocate poll_stats if there's a user of them")
Signed-off-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211202090716.3292244-1-ming.lei@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/block/blk-mq-debugfs.c b/block/blk-mq-debugfs.c
index 7f27dca3a45e..3a790eb4995c 100644
--- a/block/blk-mq-debugfs.c
+++ b/block/blk-mq-debugfs.c
@@ -30,6 +30,9 @@ static int queue_poll_stat_show(void *data, struct seq_file *m)
 	struct request_queue *q = data;
 	int bucket;
 
+	if (!q->poll_stat)
+		return 0;
+
 	for (bucket = 0; bucket < (BLK_MQ_POLL_STATS_BKTS / 2); bucket++) {
 		seq_printf(m, "read  (%d Bytes): ", 1 << (9 + bucket));
 		print_stat(m, &q->poll_stat[2 * bucket]);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `block/blk-mq-debugfs.c`**
   - **Modification:** 
     - Added a check for `q->poll_stat` at the beginning of the `queue_poll_stat_show` function. If `q->poll_stat` is not allocated (i.e., is NULL), the function returns 0 immediately, preventing any further execution that could lead to a kernel panic.

### Relationship of Modifications

- The modification addresses a potential bug that could cause a kernel panic when `queue_poll_stat_show` is called if `q->poll_stat` has not been allocated. By including the check for `q->poll_stat`, the patch ensures the function can gracefully handle the situation where the poll statistics are not available, thereby improving stability and preventing runtime errors. This fix directly relates to the previously made change indicated in the patch description, which modified the allocation logic for `poll_stat` based on its usage.

Here is the commit message:
blk-mq: check q->poll_stat in queue_poll_stat_show

Without checking q->poll_stat in queue_poll_stat_show(), kernel panic
may be caused if q->poll_stat isn't allocated.

Fixes: 48b5c1fbcd8c ("block: only allocate poll_stats if there's a user of them")
Signed-off-by: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211202090716.3292244-1-ming.lei@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `queue_poll_stat_show` function does not check if `q->poll_stat` is allocated before attempting to access it. If `q->poll_stat` is NULL, this can lead to dereferencing a null pointer, resulting in a kernel panic.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int queue_poll_stat_show(void *data, struct seq_file *m)
 {
 	struct request_queue *q = data;
 	int bucket;
 
+	if (!q->poll_stat)
+		return 0;
+
 	for (bucket = 0; bucket < (BLK_MQ_POLL_STATS_BKTS / 2); bucket++) {
 		seq_printf(m, "read  (%d Bytes): ", 1 << (9 + bucket));
 		print_stat(m, &q->poll_stat[2 * bucket]);
 		seq_puts(m, "\n");
 
 		seq_printf(m, "write (%d Bytes): ",  1 << (9 + bucket));
 		print_stat(m, &q->poll_stat[2 * bucket + 1]);
 		seq_puts(m, "\n");
 	}
 	return 0;
 }
